title: GSK全球首款乙肝功能性治愈ASO药物获批，贝普若韦生获美国FDA批准上市
content:
10月20日，葛兰素史克（GSK）宣布，反义寡核苷酸（ASO）药物 贝普若韦生（bepirovirsen）获美国FDA批准，用于联合核苷（酸）类似物逆转录酶抑制剂（NrtI）治疗慢性乙型肝炎（CHB）。图源：葛兰素史克官网贝普若韦生是GSK从Ionis Pharmaceuticals引进的创新疗法，也是慢性乙肝领域首款完成Ⅲ期临床研究的小核酸药物。该药通过靶向乙肝病毒相关RNA，降低乙肝表面抗原（HBsAg）水平，并有望激发持久的免疫应答，为慢性乙肝功能性治愈提供新的治疗选择。一、Ⅲ期研究显示，功能性治愈率达19%此次获批主要基于全球多中心Ⅲ期B-Well 1和B-Well 2研究。两项研究在全球29个国家开展，纳入接受过核苷（酸）类似物治疗、基线HBsAg水平不超过3000 IU/mL的慢性乙肝成人患者，旨在评估贝普若韦生的有效性与安全性。两项研究均达到主要终点。合并数据显示，在基线HBsAg水平不超过3000 IU/mL的患者中，接受贝普若韦生治疗6个月后，功能性治愈率达到19%（233/1220），安慰剂组为0%（0/614），两项研究的差异均具有统计学意义（P均＜0.001）。贝普若韦生部分临床试验信息图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库在基线HBsAg水平不超过1000 IU/mL的患者中，贝普若韦生的功能性治愈率进一步升至26%（200/768），安慰剂组同样为0%（0/393）。探索性分析还显示，截至第72周，全部研究人群中有49%（598/1220）的患者HBsAg水平降至100 IU/mL及以下；在基线HBsAg水平不超过1000 IU/mL的患者中，这一比例达到62%（476/768）。安全性方面，贝普若韦生总体耐受性良好，常见不良事件包括注射部位红斑、局部疼痛及血液肝酶水平暂时性升高。二、国内上市申请审评中，正大天晴已获得商业化权益在全球临床开发及商业化推进方面，贝普若韦生也取得了新的进展。2026年8月，该药首次在日本获批上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库在中国，贝普若韦生的上市申请目前正在审评中。2026年5月，中国生物制药旗下正大天晴与GSK达成合作，获得该药在中国的商业化权益。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库随着美国获批及中国上市申请推进，贝普若韦生有望进一步拓展慢性乙肝治疗选择。其在不同患者群体中的长期获益及临床应用价值，仍有待后续实践进一步验证。参考来源：[1] 企业官网/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 2026乙肝新药最新消息！GSK全球首款功能性治愈药Bepirovirsen获批上市，同日PD-1单抗获优先审评2. title: First positive phase III trial data for an individualised mRNA-based neoantigen therapy
content:
Intismeran autogene reduced the risk of recurrence by 42% in patients with resectable melanoma treated with adjuvant pembrolizumab
Patients with resectable melanoma remain at risk of recurrence despite surgery and adjuvant pembrolizumab treatment ( N Engl J Med. 2018;378:1789–1801 ; Lancet. 2022;399:1718–1729 ). Results from the phase III INTerpath-001 study , presented at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), now show that adding the individualised neoantigen therapy intismeran autogene to pembrolizumab can reduce this risk ( LBA1 ).
In this large study, recurrence-free survival (RFS), the primary endpoint, at 24 months was 82.2% in 1,137 patients treated with intismeran plus pembrolizumab versus 70.0% in those treated with placebo plus pembrolizumab (hazard ratio [HR] 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.45–0.75; p<0.001). The study also met a key secondary endpoint, with respective 24-month distant metastasis-free survival of 88.5% versus 80.2% in the intismeran and placebo arms (HR 0.62; 95% CI 0.45–0.85; p=0.002). These results are consistent with the positive results for intismeran reported in the proof-of-concept phase IIb KEYNOTE-942 trial in patients with resected melanoma ( Lancet. 2024;403:632–644 ).
“These findings mark a crucial moment in the field of cancer vaccines ,” explains Prof. Inge Marie Svane from Copenhagen University Hospital, Herlev, Denmark. “The reported HRs are convincing and show that intismeran offers additional benefit to pembrolizumab in the adjuvant setting.” Although this interim analysis showed no overall survival benefit, Svane acknowledges that this may reflect the short follow-up to date (median 24.6 months). On safety, no serious safety signals were reported. “Adverse events (AEs) were primarily fever, fatigue and injection site pain, which is typical of viral vaccines as well,” she notes. Rates of serious AEs (SAEs) and discontinuation of both agents due to AEs were similar between the intismeran and placebo groups (SAEs: 17.6% versus 15.8%; discontinuations: 6.5% versus 5.3%).
Intismeran is a highly personalised mRNA-based vaccine developed using a predictive computer algorithm based on each patient’s individual tumour cell mutations. In addition to the adjuvant melanoma setting, it is also being evaluated in first-line unresectable melanoma ( NCT06961006 ), and in other tumour types such as lung cancer ( NCT06077760 ; NCT06623422 ; NCT07513376 ) and renal cell carcinoma ( NCT06307431 ). “This is the first personalised agent designed for each patient using a computer algorithm to move through the regulatory process, and it will be very interesting to monitor its progress,” explains Svane.
Looking at the baseline characteristics of the patients in INTerpath-001, a significant proportion had stage III (C–D) or stage IV disease. Pre-specified subgroup analyses indicate that most patients benefit from the addition of intismeran, including those with more advanced disease. However, “Current guidelines recommend considering neoadjuvant therapy for these patients, so clinicians will need guidance on choosing between neoadjuvant checkpoint inhibition and adjuvant vaccine therapy,” advises Svane. There is also the potential to use intismeran as a neoadjuvant treatment. However, manufacturing time will be a challenge in this setting. “Each vaccine has to be prepared for the individual patient, which takes time and limits when it can be given. The key question is whether the vaccine can be prepared on a shorter timeline,” she explains.
In the metastatic setting, intismeran's role appears uncertain: “In patients with advanced disease, current guidelines recommend dual checkpoint inhibition as first-line treatment and it is unclear whether this mRNA-based vaccine will achieve the same level of efficacy,” Svane concludes.

title: Neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin added to peri-operative durvalumab significantly improved event-free and overall survival
content:
Results from VOLGA show that antibody–drug conjugates continue to increase treatment options for muscle-invasive bladder cancer
Recent results from the KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 and KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 trials have expanded the treatment paradigm for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) to include peri-operative nectin-4-targeted antibody–drug conjugate (ADC), enfortumab vedotin (EV), plus pembrolizumab ( N Engl J Med. 2026;394:1257–1269 ; N Engl J Med. 2026;395:338–348 ).
Today, at the Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), the first, positive phase III data were presented for neoadjuvant EV added to peri-operative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab in patients with MIBC ineligible for, or unwilling to have, cisplatin therapy ( LBA2 ). Findings from the VOLGA trial showed a significant improvement in the primary endpoint of event-free survival (EFS) for durvalumab plus EV compared with radical cystectomy (RC) alone at a median follow-up of 23 months (median EFS: not reached [NR] versus 12.1 months, respectively; hazard ratio [HR] 0.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38–0.67; p<0.0001).
At 26 months of follow-up, a significant improvement was reported in median overall survival (OS) for the durvalumab plus EV combination compared with RC alone (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.40–0.83; p=0.0027). A significant improvement in OS was not observed with the combination of durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus EV versus RC alone, although EFS was prolonged. Efficacy analyses were conducted on 233 patients in the durvalumab plus EV arm, 233 in the durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus EV arm, and 229 in the RC-only arm.
“VOLGA is clearly a positive trial in line with the KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 trial of EV plus pembrolizumab in the cisplatin-ineligible setting ( N Engl J Med. 2026;394:1257–1269 ). The KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304 trial in cisplatin-eligible patients ( N Engl J Med. 2026;395:338–348 ) prompted the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to expand the combination’s label to include peri-operative treatment of MIBC ,” comments Dr Michiel van der Heijden from the Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam, Netherlands. He notes that further investigations are now needed to determine whether EV should be used in the adjuvant setting, since it was used peri-operatively in KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 and KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304, while it was used only in the neoadjuvant setting in VOLGA.
The safety profile of durvalumab plus EV in the VOLGA trial was consistent with the profiles of the individual agents. Treatment-related adverse events known to be associated with EV included skin reactions (grade 3–4: 5%), peripheral neuropathy (grade 3–4: 0.4%) and hyperglycaemia (grade 3–4: 3%).
“Data on ADCs plus immune checkpoint inhibitors in bladder cancer are now robust and consistent, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitors and chemotherapy in bladder cancer have shown less consistency, given the negative results presented at the Congress ,” comments van der Heijden. Many ADCs are currently in development in urothelial cancer with different targets and payloads, although significant survival improvements were not observed with sacituzumab govitecan in the TROPiCS-04 trial ( Ann Oncol. 2025;36:561–571 ). “There are promising data from China with HER2-directed disitamab vedotin ( N Engl J Med. 2025;393:2324–2337 ), which taken together with data on EV suggest that the vedotin payload is particularly active in urothelial cancer. Unlike other tumour types, topoisomerase inhibition has been less successful in randomised phase III trials so far, but several late-phase clinical trials are currently ongoing ,” van der Heijden concludes.

title: Can systemic treatment intensification reduce recurrence risk in high-risk localised prostate cancer?
content:
In two phase III trials, adding an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor reduced the risk of metastasis-free survival in patients with very high risk localised or relapsed prostate cancer
“Along with the STAMPEDE trial ( Lancet. 2022;399:447–460 ), DASL-HiCaP is the second study showing that the addition of an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) results in a benefit for metastasis-free survival (MFS) when added to radiotherapy plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in patients with very high risk localised or relapsed prostate cancer,” states Prof. Silke Gillessen from Università della Svizzera Italiana and the Oncology Institute of Southern Switzerland, Bellinzona, Switzerland, commenting on findings presented at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), which support the benefits of systemic treatment intensification in very high-risk, localised and relapsed prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy ( LBA4 ).
In an interim analysis of the DASL-HiCaP study, involving 1,106 patients, darolutamide plus radiotherapy plus ADT resulted in a 4-year MFS rate by conventional imaging (MFS-CI) of 95% versus 88% for radiotherapy plus ADT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001).
Substantial improvement in MFS as well as significant improvements in secondary endpoints such as prostate-specific antigen progression-free survival (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.33–0.67) and time to subsequent hormonal therapy (HR 0.36; 95% CI 0.22–0.59) were reported. Gillessen highlights, “For our patients, the endpoint of subsequent hormonal therapy is very important, since it means having treatment again. However, excellent outcomes were also observed for patients receiving standard of care (radiotherapy plus ADT), indicating a potential benefit of modern radiotherapy techniques in this setting and that we need to understand better which patients are really profiting from treatment intensification. The patients who are at lower risk for developing metastases benefit less from the treatment intensification, which means we need to re-define ‘very high-risk’ including using biomarkers and modern imaging.”
Notably, only 4 out of 21 deaths in the darolutamide arm were due to prostate cancer. “An important message is that even in the control arm, many patients are free of metastases after 4 years. Of the patients who died, the majority died from other causes and not from prostate cancer, so for the future, we also need trials to evaluate treatment de-escalation for selected patients in this setting,” notes Gillessen.
The overall survival data (OS) are currently immature and she notes the importance of long-term follow-up : “There is evidence that MFS-CI is a surrogate marker for OS in this setting, but I am interested to see whether the addition of darolutamide translates into an OS benefit since we have made a lot of progress in the treatment of prostate cancer in the last years.”
These findings add to a growing body of evidence supporting the benefits of systemic treatment intensification in very high-risk, localised prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy and ADT. In the STAMPEDE trial , adding abiraterone and prednisolone to radiotherapy plus ADT significantly improved both MFS and OS, also in a very high-risk population ( Lancet. 2022;399:447–460 ). Conversely, in the ENZARAD study , which added enzalutamide to radiotherapy plus ADT in a high-risk population with lower risk, no significant effect on MFS was observed, although benefits were reported in subgroups of patients with positive pelvic nodes or with pelvic radiotherapy planned ( Ann Oncol. 2025;36(Suppl 2):S1628–S1629 ). Gillessen explains that differences in outcomes observed between STAMPEDE, ENZARAD, and now DASL-HiCAP most likely reflect differences in the definitions for (very) high risk for study eligibility and, more importantly, the risk profile of the included patients in the respective trials.
There is also interest in using an ARPI peri-operatively in patients with localised high-risk disease undergoing radical prostatectomy (RP). In the phase III PROTEUS study , the addition of peri-operative apalutamide to ADT was previously shown to significantly improve pathological response and MFS ( J Clin Oncol. 2026;44(Suppl 17):LBA1 ). A substudy of PROTEUS has now been conducted to evaluate the impact of adding peri-operative apalutamide to ADT in 408 patients with high-risk localised or locally advanced prostate cancer undergoing RP and pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND). As reported in Madrid, the primary endpoint was met , with event-free survival (EFS) determined by conventional or prostate-specific membrane antigen PET imaging at 36 months of 63.0% for apalutamide plus ADT versus 41.4% for RP plus PLND and local standard institutional practice (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.26–0.55; p<0.0001) ( LBA53 ).
Treatment with apalutamide plus ADT also resulted in a 51% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death (HR 0.49; 95% CI 0.26–0.90; nominal p=0.0193) and a 71% reduction in the risk of needing subsequent therapy (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.20–0.43; nominal p<0.0001). “The PROTEUS trial is probably the largest study ever conducted in this setting, which is a huge achievement,” explains Gillessen. However, there are some limitations of this substudy, including that the EFS endpoint has not been shown to be a surrogate for OS and that RP alone was not the control arm of the main study. “Interestingly in the main study, only a minority of participants in either arm was free of disease at 4 years – 22% with ADT plus apalutamide versus 18% with ADT plus placebo – suggesting that most may require additional therapy after this approach,” she clarifies.
Evidence from research on biomarkers like homologous recombination repair alterations, PTEN deficiency and PSMA PET positivity has made the approach to metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer more granular , but that same granularity is not a reality yet in the high-risk, localised setting. “It is now clear that some patients do not need treatment intensification, while others do, but we still need to identify who really benefits,” Gillessen concludes.

title: Novel first-line treatment significantly improves outcomes in small cell lung cancer
content:
Positive findings from adding tarlatamab to durvalumab maintenance in the  DeLLphi-305 trial are potentially practice-changing
“The survival gains observed with the addition of tarlatamab to durvalumab first-line maintenance are of a magnitude not previously seen in small cell lung cancer (SCLC),” says Dr Stephen Liu from Georgetown Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center, Georgetown University, Washington, DC, US, commenting on the positive results from the phase III DeLLphi-305 trial presented at today’s Presidential Symposium at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) ( LBA3 ). As reported, the addition of the bispecific T-cell engager immunotherapy, tarlatamab, to maintenance durvalumab significantly improved the primary endpoint of overall survival (OS) compared with durvalumab alone in patients with extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC).
SCLC is a subtype of lung cancer that predictably relapses despite good responses to initial therapy. The standard treatment at relapse is topotecan chemotherapy, but this is associated with dismal outcomes: OS rates at 6 and 12 months of <40% and <10% in refractory patients ( Sci Rep. 2015;5:15437 ). While novel therapies are being developed for use in later treatment lines, many patients do not receive these agents as they are no longer fit for further therapy following relapse; therefore, developing more effective early-line treatments is essential.
In the DeLLphi-305 trial, the pre-specified interim analysis at a median follow-up of 15.9 months and 16.1 months for the two treatment arms revealed a median OS of 21.1 months for tarlatamab plus durvalumab versus 12.7 months for durvalumab alone (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.32–0.54; p<0.001). Significant improvements in median progression-free survival (PFS; 7.4 months versus 1.9 months; HR 0.34; 95% CI 0.28–0.42; p<0.001) and objective response rate (26.4% versus 4.1%; p<0.001) were also observed with the combination.
These results follow previous demonstrations of improved OS and PFS for tarlatamab compared with topotecan and other chemotherapies as second-line treatment in the phase III DeLLphi-304 trial ( N Engl J Med. 2025;393:349–361 ) and also promising anticancer activity in combination with immunotherapy as first-line therapy in the phase Ib DeLLphi-303 study ( Lancet Oncol. 2025;26:1300–1311 ), suggesting that outcomes could be improved with proactive delivery prior to relapse.
Previously, the longest median OS for first-line treatment of ES-SCLC was 13.2 months with lurbinectedin added to atezolizumab maintenance in the phase III IMforte trial ( Lancet. 2025;405:2129–2143 ). “The improvement in median PFS from 1.9 months to 7.4 months with the tarlatamab combination is also profound; to keep this cancer from relapsing for that period is quite remarkable,” Liu adds.
Although a doubling of grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) was reported with the tarlatamab plus durvalumab combination (20.9%) compared with durvalumab alone (10.8%), Liu is reassured that the additional toxicity does not appear to adversely impact drug delivery; the rate of discontinuation of durvalumab due to TRAEs was low in both arms (3.2% and 3.6%). Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune-effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome – toxicities specifically associated with bispecific T-cell engagers – occurred in 49.6% and 1.1% of patients in the combination arm. However, these were almost entirely grade 1; only 1 patient discontinued (due to CRS) and there were no fatal cases. The safety findings align with a recent update to the U.S. label to reduce monitoring requirements for tarlatamab from 22–24 hours to 6–8 hours from the start of the first 2 infusions. “This paves the way for safe use of the agent in an outpatient setting and will overcome some of the existing barriers to delivery and access,” notes Liu.
The data support the tarlatamab plus durvalumab combination as a new standard of care first-line maintenance therapy in ES-SCLC. However, other novel therapies are also showing promise in this setting, including the anti-B7-H3 antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) tambotatug pelitecan and risvutatug rezetecan that have demonstrated survival benefits compared with topotecan in patients with relapsed SCLC in the phase III TAISHAN-302 and ARTEMIS-008 studies ( N Engl J Med. 2026 doi: 10.1056/NEJMoa2610229 ; IASLC 2026, PL02.04). “These ADCs are clearly superior to topotecan and will provide important second-line options if tarlatamab moves successfully into the first-line space. Looking to the future, these agents could also potentially move to the first-line setting and provide effective partners for immunotherapy and tarlatamab. The field is continuing to evolve, and these are exciting times for SCLC,” Liu concludes.

title: A simplified regimen preserved efficacy and reduced toxicity in metastatic colorectal cancer
content:
Bi-weekly dosing of trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab was associated with similar overall survival and lower haematological adverse events than the conventional dosing regimen
“Results from the PRABITAS trial show that bi-weekly dosing improves safety but without compromising efficacy, establishing a new standard treatment option,” comments Dr Guillem Argilés from the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, USA, who welcomes findings presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October) ( LBA31 ). In the phase III study, the primary endpoint of noninferiority in overall survival (OS) was met with bi-weekly and conventional dosing of trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab in 970 patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer . Median OS was 11.3 months with bi-weekly trifluridine–tipiracil (35 mg/m 2 BID, days 1–5) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg IV, day 1) and 10.3 months with conventional trifluridine–tipiracil (35 mg/m 2 BID, days 1–5 and days 8–12) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg IV, days 1 and 15) (hazard [HR] 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.80–1.08; p<0.0001 for noninferiority). Superiority was not demonstrated.
Importantly, the bi-weekly regimen was associated with an improved safety profile . Haematological treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were significantly reduced with bi-weekly versus conventional dosing including grade ≥3 neutropenia (13% versus 39%) and leukopenia (7% versus 18%). Grade ≥3 anorexia, nausea and diarrhoea were also significantly reduced with bi-weekly versus conventional dosing.
“The conventional trifluridine–tipiracil plus bevacizumab regimen was established based on results from the SUNLIGHT trial ( N Engl J Med. 2023;388:1657–1667 ), but tolerability issues, particularly anorexia, nausea and vomiting, have limited its effectiveness in clinical practice where patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer have already had to deal with several treatment lines,” he adds.
Data on the impact of bi-weekly dosing on quality of life were not presented but this may be due to the pragmatic design and streamlined data collection, which aimed to reduce the burden on patients and healthcare providers. The trial had broad eligibility criteria and flexibility around dose modification and chemotherapy timing. Dose reductions were found to be lower with bi-weekly versus conventional dosing (31% versus 48%), cycle delays were less frequent (58% versus 68%) and the median relative dose intensity was numerically higher with bi-weekly dosing (83% versus 77%).
Argilés points to the ReDOS and REARRANGE trials , which assessed dosing modification strategies with regorafenib, as other examples of post-marketing academic-led efforts that have successfully sought to optimise dosing ( Lancet Oncol. 2019;20:1070–1082 ; Eur J Cancer. 2022;177:154–163 ). He notes that the dosing schedules used in phase III trials have often been chosen to “maximise the demonstration of efficacy” and are based on doses from phase I trials in a small number of selected patients. “In many cases, recommendations on dosing do not reflect what patients can actually tolerate in real-world practice, leading to the need for post-approval trials to determine an acceptable dose modification that is suitable for the broader population seen in the clinic. Earlier attempts to optimise the safety profile of new treatments would be beneficial,” he concludes.

title: Adding Abiraterone to ADT and Docetaxel Improves Survival in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
content:
After almost eight years of follow-up in the phase 3 PEACE-1 trial, adding abiraterone to standard treatment for men whose prostate cancer had already spread at diagnosis reduced the risk of death by 25%.
In men also receiving docetaxel chemotherapy, 40.3% were alive at eight years with abiraterone versus 27.1% without it.
Survival outcomes favoured triplet therapy in both low- and high-volume metastatic prostate cancer, and the benefit did not differ significantly between the two groups.
Lugano/Madrid – Adding abiraterone to standard treatment provides a lasting survival benefit for men whose prostate cancer has already spread at diagnosis, reinforcing the value of early treatment intensification. The findings come from almost eight years of follow-up in the academically led phase 3 PEACE-1 trial presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 . (1)
For men with de novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC), treatment is based on androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) to lower testosterone. Adding docetaxel chemotherapy or a second-generation hormonal therapy, such as abiraterone, improves survival, with a direct comparison finding no significant difference in overall survival between the two doublet regimens. (2)
The PEACE-1 trial included 1,173 men with de novo mCSPC. All received standard of care (ADT, with or without docetaxel chemotherapy) and were randomly assigned to receive no additional treatment, abiraterone plus prednisone, radiotherapy to the prostate, or both abiraterone plus prednisone and radiotherapy. Overall, 57% had high-volume disease, indicating more extensive cancer spread. An earlier analysis showed that adding abiraterone to standard of care improved overall survival. (3)
After a median follow-up of 7.7 years, adding abiraterone reduced the risk of death by 25% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65–0.87; p=0.0001). Median overall survival was 6.1 years with abiraterone versus 4.6 years without it.
Among the 710 men who received ADT plus docetaxel (doublet therapy), adding abiraterone plus prednisone (triplet therapy) reduced the risk of death by 32% (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.56–0.82). Median survival was 6.2 years with triplet therapy versus 4.4 years with doublet therapy, and 40.3% versus 27.1% of men were alive at eight years.
The survival benefit of triplet therapy did not differ significantly by extent of disease (interaction test p=0.56). In men with high-volume disease, median survival was 4.6 years with triplet therapy versus 3.5 years with doublet therapy (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.54–0.85), and almost twice as many were alive at eight years (38% vs 20%). In men with low-volume disease, median survival was 7.8 years with triplet therapy versus 6.2 years with doublet therapy (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.52–1.05), although this difference was not statistically significant on its own.
Among men in the control groups whose cancer progressed, 86% went on to receive an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI), the same class of treatment as abiraterone. The investigators suggest this supports starting treatment early rather than waiting until progression. No new long-term safety concerns were identified. Among men who received doublet or triplet therapy without radiotherapy, grade 3-4 high blood pressure occurred in 21% with triplet therapy versus 14% with doublet therapy, and grade 3-4 low potassium levels in 4% versus 1%.
“There is a major survival benefit, with almost two years of additional life for patients receiving the three treatments, which is of course highly significant,” said lead author Dr Karim Fizazi, Centre Oscar Lambret, Lille, France. “In our opinion, this makes this triplet treatment a strong standard of care for these patients.”
“Most clinical trials, especially when led by pharma companies, tend to stop their follow-up early,” Fizazi added. “This long-term analysis demonstrated that the survival benefit becomes greater with time: for instance, in men with multiple metastases at diagnosis, there are almost twice as many long-term survivors with triplet therapy.”
“For patients and clinicians, these data mean that modern, intensified systemic treatment – particularly triplet therapy with ADT, docetaxel and abiraterone – can translate into a substantially improved chance of long-term disease control and survival, with toxicity that is generally manageable,” said Dr Ursula Vogl, Oncology Institute of Southern Switzerland (IOSI), Bellinzona, Switzerland, who was not involved in the study.
PEACE-1 did not directly compare triplet therapy with ADT plus a newer hormone therapy without chemotherapy, which is another treatment option. Vogl explained that the decision to add docetaxel therefore depends on individual patient factors, including other health conditions, age and preferences. She emphasised that it remains unclear which patients gain the greatest additional benefit from chemotherapy, highlighting the need for personalised treatment selection.

title: Intensifying treatment in hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: long follow-up data confirm overall survival benefits
content:
Updated analyses from the phase III CAPItello-281 and PEACE-1 studies reveal significant improvements with the addition of capivasertib to abiraterone and abiraterone to standard of care
“The treatment landscape in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) is rapidly expanding, with many strategies to intensify treatment on top of an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) showing positive results in clinical trials,” notes Dr Elena Castro from Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre, Madrid, Spain, following the presentation of long-term overall survival (OS) improvements with treatment intensification at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October).
The CAPItello-281 trial was previously reported to meet its primary endpoint of radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) with greater benefit when more stringent cut-offs were used. However, at the time of the primary analysis, no significant improvement in OS was observed with the addition of capivasertib to abiraterone acetate ( Ann Oncol. 2026;37:53–68 ). After an additional 17 months of follow-up (and 42% OS maturity), median OS was 57.4 months with the AKT inhibitor combination therapy versus 46.5 months with placebo plus abiraterone (hazard ratio [HR] 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68–0.99; p=0.044) in 1,012 patients with PTEN-deficient mHSPC) ( LBA56 , key results in the box below). Notably, the differences in treatment effect previously observed across PTEN deficiency cut-offs appeared less pronounced with longer follow-up, with treatment effects becoming more similar across the different biomarker thresholds evaluated.
Median rPFS was 35.5 months versus 26.0 months (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.70–0.99; p=0.033). “It is well established that PTEN deficiency results in worse outcomes when treated with a conventional ARPI, and these updated results are consistent with a clinically meaningful benefit from the addition of capivasertib to abiraterone in this population,” adds Castro.
In a second study – the PEACE-1 trial involving 1,172 patients with mHSPC – median OS was 4.6 years with standard of care (SOC) and 6.1 years with SOC plus abiraterone (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65–0.87; p=0.0001) at a long-term median follow-up of 7.7 years ( Abstract 2215O , key results in the box below). In the subgroup of patients treated with ADT plus docetaxel as SOC, adding abiraterone increased median OS from 4.4 years to 6.2 years (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.56–0.82; p<0.0001). The primary data have already changed the SOC for patients with mHSPC as the study demonstrated the superiority of adding abiraterone to docetaxel plus ADT, particularly in patients with high-volume disease ( Lancet. 2022;399:1695–1707 ), but updated results provide further strength. “An almost 2-year increase in OS with the addition of abiraterone to docetaxel was reported, and the magnitude of the difference has increased over time. Interestingly, no evidence of heterogeneity of treatment effect according to disease volume has been noted, suggesting a benefit from treatment intensification in the low-volume population, also. However, PEACE-1 was not designed to determine the incremental value of docetaxel when added to contemporary ARPI-based therapy. Therefore, although these results support the efficacy of triplet treatment , they do not resolve whether all fit patients receiving an ARPI require concomitant docetaxel,” notes Castro.
Currently, treatment decisions are informed by a fragmented evidence base and results from trials of other strategies are still emerging. Prolonged rPFS has been observed with lutetium-177 radioligand therapy for patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-expressing tumours ( Lancet. 2026;408:793–807 ), while PARP inhibitors have shown benefits in patients with homologous recombination repair (HRR) alterations ( Nat Med. 2025;31:4109–4118 ; N Engl J Med. 2026;395:427–439 ). At the same time, response-adapted approaches are also being tested: either treatment escalation, where patients treated on ADT plus an ARPI have chemotherapy added only if the initial prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response is inadequate ( NCT06592924 ), or de-escalation, where treatment with ADT plus an ARPI is stopped in patients who respond well ( NCT05974774 ). Finally, the role of metastases-directed therapy in oligometastatic patients is also being addressed in several trials.
“ Early treatment is critical to maximise the duration of symptom control and long-term survival. Yet, with several effective intensification approaches now available, the next challenge is determining how best to personalise treatments and identify which therapeutic components are truly necessary for individual patients. As clinical, molecular and imaging-based criteria often converge, many patients may qualify for multiple evidence-based approaches. Defining the incremental value of each treatment modality will be essential to optimise outcomes while avoiding unnecessary treatment burden,” concludes Castro.

title: Atirmociclib extends progression-free survival by three months in endocrine-resistant metastatic breast cancer
content:
In FOURLIGHT-1, the next-generation CDK4 inhibitor also led to a greater objective response rate and longer duration of response in previously-treated women compared with standard of care
As reported at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), the phase II FOURLIGHT-1 study (N=263) showed a statistically significant benefit in investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS; primary endpoint) in patients with hormone receptor (HR)-positive/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer (mBC) treated with atirmociclib plus fulvestrant (n=126) versus investigator’s choice of standard therapy (ICT [n=137]; fulvestrant alone or everolimus plus exemestane) ( Abstract 1842O ). Considering that all women involved in the study had already received a CDK4/6 inhibitor, “Extending median PFS by approximately 3 months with a further CDK inhibitor suggests this agent is providing superior cell-cycle control,” comments Dr Peter Fasching from University Hospital Erlangen and Comprehensive Cancer Center Erlangen-EMN, Germany.
Atirmociclib (PF-07220060), a first-in-class , next-generation CDK4-selective cell-cycle inhibitor , has previously shown encouraging antitumour activity and tolerability in combination with endocrine therapy in early-phase trials of HR-positive/HER2-negative mBC ( Clin Cancer Res. 2025;31(Suppl 12):P5-07-28 ; ESMO Open. 2024;9(Suppl 4):103206 ).
In the study, median PFS was 9.4 months with atirmociclib plus fulvestrant versus 6.6 months with ICT (hazard ratio 0.60; 95% confidence interval 0.440–0.825; p=0.0007). Fasching notes that the median PFS of 6.6 months reported in the control arm seems relatively high for this endocrine-resistant population: “Based on historical data, we would normally expect PFS of 3–4 months with fulvestrant. Prolonging this to almost 10 months with atirmociclib is, however, a marked and clinically quite meaningful improvement over standard therapy.” Patients treated with atirmociclib also experienced a greater objective response rate (19.3% versus 11.3%; p=0.0901), longer duration of response (median 14.8 months versus 9.3 months) and increased clinical benefit rate (61.9% versus 46.0%; p=0.0083) compared with the control arm. Overall survival (OS) data were not mature at data cut-off.
The relatively favourable safety profile of atirmociclib appears to be as expected based on extensive experience with cell-cycle control agents for more than a decade. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in the atirmociclib arm were neutropenia (47%) and leukopenia (34%), and 6.4% of patients discontinued atirmociclib due to TEAEs.
FOURLIGHT-1 is the first randomised study to provide an insight into the impact of superior cell-cycle control on clinical response in an endocrine-resistant population with mBC. The emergence of resistance mutations ( PIK3CA , ESR1 ) and duration of response in the first-line setting are factors that usually complicate disease management in this setting ( Cancer Treat Rev. 2025;138:102972 ). In the control arm of FOURLIGHT-1, 35% of patients had an ESR1 mutation and 45% had alterations in the PI3K pathway. The recently-released ESMO Living Guideline in Metastatic Breast Cancer highlights how genomic biomarkers, including ESR1 , PIK3CA , AKT1 , PTEN and BRCA1/2 can guide therapy post-CDK4/6 inhibitors ( Ann Oncol. 2026;37:1203–1219 ; ESMO Living Guideline: Metastatic Breast Cancer, v2.0 August 2026 ). While permitted in the study, the proportion of patients who received prior biomarker-directed therapy is not reported. Therefore, it could be argued that the control arm in FOURLIGHT-1 would not be considered standard in clinical practice.
A further potential limitation of the study is the selection of fulvestrant as the endocrine combination partner, as other agents have shown greater activity with cell-cycle inhibitors, including novel epigenetic inhibitors ( Am Soc Clin Oncol Educ Book. 2025;45:e473372 ) and oral selective oestrogen receptor degraders ( Breast. 2024;75:103729 ). The latter include giredestrant, that demonstrated a median PFS of 10.0 months when combined with everolimus in the evERA study ( N Engl J Med. 2026;395:1285–1298 ), and imlunestrant, that achieved a median PFS of 10.9 months when combined with abemaciclib in the EMBER-3 trial ( Ann Oncol. 2026;37:532–543 ). Both studies were conducted in patients with endocrine-resistant advanced or mBC, although cross-trial comparisons should be avoided.
“But this study’s results are reassuring and provide proof of principle to inform future clinical development , including treatment in earlier lines,” adds Fasching. “For patients with early-stage disease , the treatment could potentially provide survival benefits, and this would take next-generation cell-cycle control agents to the next level.”
The FOURLIGHT-3 phase III study is currently underway to evaluate first-line atirmociclib versus CDK4/6 inhibitor (both with letrozole) in patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative mBC. Further research investigating atirmociclib combinations may help fully characterise its clinical activity.

content:
10月19日，葛兰素史克（GSK）宣布，美国FDA加速批准其抗PD-1抗体Dostarlimab一项新适应症，用于治疗II期和III期微卫星不稳定性高（MSI-H）/错配修复缺陷（dMMR）局部晚期直肠癌成人患者。图源：葛兰素史克官网据GSK介绍，Dostarlimab是美国首个且目前唯一获批用于该患者群体的免疫疗法。此次获批主要基于II期AZUR-1研究结果，数据显示，接受治疗的患者中，近七成持续实现完全临床缓解。一、II期临床数据公布，近七成患者持续缓解AZUR-1是一项全球性、开放标签、单臂注册性II期临床试验，共纳入154例既往未经治疗的II/III期dMMR/MSI-H局部晚期直肠癌患者。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库研究评估了Dostarlimab单药治疗的疗效，给药方案为500mg、每3周一次静脉注射。主要终点为治疗后12个月内持续实现完全临床缓解（cCR12）的患者比例。研究结果显示，在可评估疗效的患者中：研究者评估：144例患者中，98例达到cCR12，比例为68%。探索性分析：144例患者中，110例在治疗至少1年后无癌症迹象，占76%。其中，98例未接受手术即达到cCR12，另有12例在手术后达到cCR12。独立中央审评：116例患者中，54例达到cCR12，比例为47%；另有38例仍处于12个月随访期，且已实现完全临床缓解。完全临床缓解意味着临床评估未发现肿瘤残留证据，并不等同于已证实治愈。此次研究结果为Dostarlimab在局部晚期dMMR/MSI-H直肠癌中的应用提供了进一步临床依据。二、年销售额超11亿美元，Dostarlimab持续放量Dostarlimab是一款靶向程序性死亡受体1（PD-1）的单克隆抗体，通过阻断PD-1通路，帮助恢复机体针对肿瘤细胞的免疫反应。该药于2021年4月首次在全球获批上市，此后逐步拓展适应症，应用领域涵盖子宫内膜癌、实体瘤及结直肠癌等。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库销售方面，Dostarlimab在2025年实现全球销售额11.36亿美元，同比增长90.56%，成为GSK肿瘤业务的重要产品之一。此次直肠癌新适应症获FDA加速批准，有望进一步拓展其在肿瘤免疫治疗领域的应用空间。三、中国尚未上市，相关临床研究仍在推进除静脉注射剂型外，GSK还在开发Dostarlimab皮下注射剂型，目前正在开展针对子宫内膜癌的Ⅰ/Ⅱ期临床试验。在中国，Dostarlimab尚未获批上市。目前，该药针对结肠癌、头颈部鳞状细胞癌及非小细胞肺癌的Ⅲ期临床研究正在开展。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库随着此次FDA批准落地，Dostarlimab在dMMR/MSI-H局部晚期直肠癌中的应用进一步拓展，其后续临床开发及在不同市场的注册进展值得关注。参考来源：[1] 企业官网/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. title: Next-generation bispecific antibody–ADC combinations show promise across several tumours
content:
Three early-phase studies report anticancer activity and manageable safety of elfetabart drozuntecan plus pumitamig and of a novel bispecific ADC targeting EGFR and either cMET or B7H3
Bispecific antibodies with dual targets are emerging as an attractive combination partner for antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs), offering distinct but complementary mechanisms that may further enhance immune activity ( iScience. 2025;28:114203 ). Either administered as separate agents or as bispecific ADCs (BsADCs) – an antibody scaffold with two antigen-binding sites conjugated to a cytotoxic payload – the bispecific–ADC strategy has demonstrated an efficacy signal across several tumour types, albeit in small patient numbers, according to results reported at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October).
“There is growing excitement around the ADC target B7H3, which is over-expressed in many tumours and has been receiving much attention recently, and these study data provide further support,” says Dr Funda Meric-Bernstam from the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, TX, USA, commenting on the results. Promising first results were presented from a phase II study exploring the investigational B7H3-targeting ADC, elfetabart drozuntecan, in combination with the investigational anti-PD-L1 and VEGF-A bispecific antibody, pumitamig ( Abstract 999O , key results in the box below). The combination was well tolerated, with no dose-limiting toxicities and no drug-related fatal events in 142 patients with advanced solid tumours. Anticancer activity was also demonstrated across patient cohorts with various tumour types, including head and neck cancer (n=39; objective response rate [ORR] 38.5%), melanoma (n=26; ORR 30.8%), hepatocellular carcinoma (n=21; ORR 42.9%), cervical cancer (n=22; ORR 50.0%) and platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (n=31; ORR 80.6%), and was also observed in patients pre-treated with immunotherapy or bevacizumab, with data broadly comparable to the overall population.
“At the data cut-off for this first analysis, most patients remained on treatment for ≥6 months and only 3.5% had discontinued due to treatment-related adverse events, which is promising. It will be important to see that deep and durable responses and few discontinuations are maintained in the longer term,” Meric-Bernstam comments.
By incorporating two targets (two epitopes on the same receptor or two different tumour-associated antigens), BsADCs are proposed to have several advantages over traditional single-target ADCs, including enhanced sensitivity and internalisation, clinical activity despite tumour heterogeneity, and the potential for increased tumour-specific binding with reduced off-tumour toxicities ( Exp Hematol Oncol. 2025;14:33 ; Cancer Chemother Pharmacol. 2026;96:15 ).
Encouraging activity and manageable safety with novel BsADCs targeting EGFR and either cMET or B7H3 were reported from two phase I studies at the ESMO Congress. The EGFR/cMET bispecific antibody conjugated to a topoisomerase I (TOP1) inhibitor payload was associated with an ORR of 55.7% and disease control rate (DCR) of 92.5% in the largest patient cohort (n=106) with EGFR -mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with an increased ORR (61.3%) and a 6-month PFS rate of 75.3% in patients who received a 6 mg/kg dose (n=31) ( Abstract 1000O , key results in the box below). Activity was also observed in other tumour types, including nasopharyngeal cancer (n=6; ORR, 66.7%; DCR, 83.3%) although the cohorts were small.
The EGFR/B7H3 bispecific antibody , also with a TOP1 inhibitor payload, demonstrated activity across several solid tumours, including EGFR -mutant NSCLC (n=16; ORR 31.3%; median progression-free survival [mPFS] 7.7 months), small cell lung cancer (n=8; ORR 62.5%), head and neck and oesophageal squamous cell carcinomas (n=5; ORR 60.0%), and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (n=15; mPFS 6.9 months) ( Abstract 1001O , key results in the box below).
Since both studies included patients with advanced solid tumours regardless of biomarker status, Meric-Bernstam cautions that further data on the impact of biomarker expression are awaited: “It will be especially important to determine the relative efficacy of these agents when 1 or 2 bispecific targets are present. Currently, it is unknown whether expression of both targets is required for optimal internalisation or if expression of 1 bispecific target is sufficient for optimal clinical activity.”
ADCs have been associated with significant activity, particularly in solid tumours such as breast, lung and urothelial cancers ( Front Pharmacol. 2025;16:1556245 ), and multiple ADC agents have now been approved for cancer therapy. However, resistance continues to be a major obstacle to successful treatment, and the potential for combination with immunotherapy to enhance activity and response durability is being actively explored ( Cancer Res. 2026;86(Suppl 7):5655 ; Front Pharmacol. 2025;16:1556245 ). “Further research will be needed to address several critical questions relating to the optimal ADC target and most suitable combination partner for each disease type and patient, and the added value of bispecific immunotherapy compared with traditional immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations,” she concludes. “Ultimately, larger studies will be needed over the next few years to answer these challenging questions, and this will require a community-driven approach to better understand how treatment choices can be individualised.”

title: Preliminary data support encorafenib and cetuximab rechallenge in metastatic colorectal cancer
content:
Results from three studies are encouraging, but optimal patient selection and treatment strategies remain to be elucidated
Based on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) benefits reported in the phase III BEACON and BREAKWATER trials ( N Engl J Med. 2019;381:1632–1643 ; Nat Med. 2025;31:901–908 ), the standard of care for BRAF V600-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is currently chemotherapy combined with the BRAF inhibitor encorafenib and the EGFR inhibitor cetuximab (EC). Although resistance to these therapies typically develops due to genomic mutations, evidence suggests that these alterations recede upon treatment withdrawal ( Nat Med. 2015;21:795–801 ), providing a rationale for rechallenging patients with EC after a treatment break.
“ Treatment rechallenge may be a good therapeutic option for selected patients, and in clinical practice we observe some disease response or an improvement in symptoms, such as pain reduction, as a result of this approach,” explains Dr Rona Yaeger from the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, USA. “However, research is needed to identify which patients are likely to benefit from rechallenge and to determine optimal treatment combinations and dosing schedules .”
Encouraging findings from three studies evaluating the benefits of EC rechallenge in patients with BRAF V600-mutant mCRC were reported at the ESMO Congress 2026 (Madrid, 23–27 October), which continue to support rechallenge as a possibility despite a lack of conclusive answers to the many unanswered questions in this area.
In the phase II TRIDENTE study, 21 patients who experienced disease progression on EC were rechallenged with EC plus the MEK inhibitor binimetinib after a treatment break of at least 4 months, achieving an objective response rate of 19%, with partial response (PR) in 4 patients ( Abstract 789RO , key results in the box below). “These findings are encouraging and the data are consistent with the concept that tumours can quickly develop resistance following an initial treatment response. However, the study is small and PFS was short at only 2.8 months,” notes Yaeger. “Also, the study only included patients who achieved at least a PR to initial treatment, which may have resulted in the selection of a patient population most likely to respond to rechallenge.”
Similar results were reported from the ECLYPse phase II trial , which evaluated EC plus FOLFIRI in 25 patients who had previously progressed on second-line EC after initially achieving a complete response (CR), PR or stable disease (SD) lasting at least 3 months ( Abstract 788RO , key results in the box below). Overall, 14 disease progression events occurred, median PFS was 7.1 months, and median OS was not reached. “Overall, these patients responded well,” adds Yaeger. “However, it is unclear whether the response relates to the addition of chemotherapy or to the rechallenge with EC. This study would also benefit from circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) monitoring to determine changes in resistance over time.”
In contrast to the TRIDENTE and ECLYPse studies, there was no signal for activity with EC rechallenge in 16 eligible patients in the phase II BRICKET trial , with no objective responses, a median PFS of 2.9 months and median OS of 9.1 months ( Abstract 787RO , key results in the box below). “This lack of response may be partially due to the eligibility criteria, which only required patients to have stable disease following initial EC treatment, while TRIDENTE had stricter criteria, requiring patients to have at least a PR to initial treatment,” she explains. Yaeger also notes that patients in TRIDENTE may have benefited from the addition of MEK inhibition, whereas patients in BRICKET only received EC. “At this stage, it is unclear to what extent binimetinib contributed to the favourable responses reported in TRIDENTE,” she adds.
Taken together, these findings support the concept that not all patients will benefit from rechallenge and underscores the need to identify the patients who are most likely to respond, but more solid results are needed to define specifications around rechallenge , including the optimal time interval between targeted treatments, the minimum level of response to initial therapy and whether resistance-coding alterations are detected in ctDNA.

title: Cell：肠道菌代谢物决定 CAR-T细胞成败！戊酸助阵、吲哚拖后腿，代谢风险评分可预测疗效
content:
Cell：肠道菌代谢物决定 CAR-T细胞成败！戊酸助阵、吲哚拖后腿，代谢风险评分可预测疗效
来源：生物谷原创 2026-10-21 10:47
这项研究为肠道微生物组在CAR-T细胞疗法中的作用提供了新视角。
免疫疗法，尤其是 CAR-T细胞疗法，近年来从根本上改变了癌症治疗，特别是某些形式的白血病和淋巴瘤。然而，并非所有肿瘤都同样反应良好，其原因仍未被完全理解。莱布尼茨免疫治疗研究所合作组 Innate Immune Sensing in Cancer and Transplantation 的一项新多中心研究现在表明，决定CAR-T细胞疗法成功的不仅是肠道微生物群的组成，而尤其是其代谢产物。
正如发表在 Cell 期刊上所述，某些微生物代谢物可以增强或抑制CAR-T细胞功能，对治疗结局产生重大影响。它们还为基于微生物组的疗法和旨在癌症治疗期间支持肠道微生物组的饮食策略提供了起点。
这项研究以来自 Munich (LMU)、Heidelberg 和 Regensburg 的 3 所德国大学医院的 129 名患者的观察性队列为中心。使用先进的微生物组和代谢组分析，研究团队鉴定了与 CAR-T细胞疗法应答或失败相关的肠道微生物组代谢物。
然后在小鼠模型和使用人类CAR-T细胞的临床前模型中测试了这些代谢物。这使研究人员能够分析它们对CAR-T细胞活性、代谢和疗效的直接影响，并首次更详细地阐明潜在生物学机制。
“我们的结果表明，单个微生物代谢物可以产生非常不同的影响，因此如果未来要利用肠道微生物组来预测或改善治疗成功，就需要具体考虑它们，”Hendrik Poeck 说。
特别值得注意的是短链脂肪酸戊酸：治疗前水平低与疾病进展风险更高相关，而治疗性给药改善了人类和小鼠模型中的CAR-T细胞功能。
相比之下，吲哚代谢物如吲哚-3-甲醛（Indole-3-carboxaldehyde） 和‌吲哚-3-乙酸‌（indole-3-acetic acid ） 水平升高与不利结局相关；这些代谢物在人类和小鼠模型中都降低了CAR-T细胞疗效。异戊酸，一种支链脂肪酸，被证明更复杂：它在某些方面改善了CAR-T细胞功能，但也与一种此前未知的促肿瘤作用相关。
微生物组复杂性：对免疫系统和肿瘤都有影响
这项研究为肠道微生物组在CAR-T细胞疗法中的作用提供了新视角。直到现在，研究主要集中在细菌组成上。这项工作反而表明，微生物代谢物是影响治疗成功的关键生物学角色。研究还表明，这些代谢物并非本质上就有益或有害；它们可以产生高度特异性、有时相反的效果。
“这些发现突出了微生物组的矛盾性和复杂性：它不仅影响治疗性免疫系统，也影响肿瘤本身，”Poeck 说。
“通过我们的研究，我们挑战了一个此前占主导地位的观点，并为微生物组研究和基于微生物组疗法的进一步发展开辟了新视角，”Dr. Dr. Markus Perl 说，他是第一作者，也是 University Hospital Regensburg 的医师。从长远来看，这些结果可能有助于通过靶向调节肠道微生物组来改善免疫疗法结局，例如通过微生物群转移或特定饮食策略。
“基于这些发现，我们目前正在 NCT-OCT2 项目中准备一项临床试验 CARBiome，研究在接受过抗生素并计划接受CAR-T细胞疗法的多发性骨髓瘤患者中进行微生物群转移，”Dr. Erik Thiele-Orberg, Ph.D. 说，他是该研究的共同最后作者。
Perl 补充说，这项研究还表明，“Regensburg 科学中心卓越的、具有国际可见度的前沿研究之所以成功，要归功于强有力的合作以及全世界许多敬业科学家的共同努力。”
微生物组研究转向生物活性代谢物
“这些发现将CAR-T细胞疗法中的微生物组研究从纯粹的细菌组成观点转向生物活性代谢物，”Dr. Severin Gütter 和 Dr. Simon Holzinger 解释说，两人都是该研究的共同第一作者。
“我们希望，聚焦细菌代谢物将能够在未来实现更稳健的治疗成功生物标志物。此外，这些代谢物的靶向治疗使用为未来治疗开辟了有趣前景，例如使CAR-T细胞疗法更有效。”
研究团队已经为临床应用提供了初步概念验证：一种基于代谢物的风险评分预测了对CAR-T细胞疗法的临床应答。下一步是与国家和国际伙伴合作，在额外队列中验证这些发现。（生物谷Bioon.com）

content:
2026年10月15日，Verastem Oncology公布了口服KRAS G12D抑制剂VS-7375治疗晚期KRAS G12D突变实体瘤的1/2期TARGET-D 101研究最新数据。 在接受900 mg每日一次VS-7375单药治疗的二线胰腺导管腺癌（PDAC）患者中，确认客观缓解率（ORR）达到50%（4/8）；在二线及后线患者整体中，确认ORR为41%（9/22），并观察到2例完全缓解，其中1例已得到确认。 安全性方面，在48例接受900 mg每日一次单药治疗的患者中，因不良事件停药的比例为2%，3级治疗相关不良事件发生率为10%，未观察到具有临床意义的累积毒性。

content:

小核酸药物在过去五年迎来了管线的爆发式增长，但高速推进的另一面是同样不容忽视的失败率。全球1368个小核酸项目中，处于研发失败、停滞或拒绝上市状态的有455个，失败率约33.3%。2021年以来，259个管线进入失败或停滞状态，其中64.4%终止于药物发现或临床前阶段。更值得深思的是，一些管线在临床试验中成功实现了靶点调控——poly(GP)下降了48%，ATXN2蛋白显著降低，外显子跳跃水平优于已上市药物——却依然未能走到终点。靶点被成功调控，并不意味着疾病进程能够被改变；药效成立之后，安全窗口与产品价值仍决定研发成败。本文内容整理自摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》报告，结合摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库对全球小核酸项目全生命周期追踪能力，系统梳理近五年研发失败管线的结构性特征与代表性案例。摩熵医药数据库覆盖药物从靶点发现到临床终止的完整信息链条，为行业研究者识别“陷阱靶点”、理解失败逻辑、优化立项决策提供了可验证的数据底座。一、近五年小核酸药物研发失败管线：终止阶段与失败原因分布作为新兴生物技术，小核酸药物的开发仍存在诸多困难。据摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库统计，在全球1368个小核酸药物项目中，处于研发失败、无后续进展、拒绝上市等失败状态的有455个，研发失败率约33.3%。1. 研发失败风险前置近五年行业研发失败的风险呈现明显前置特征，大量管线的终止集中在早期转化与临床价值验证阶段。2021年以来，共有259个研发管线进入了研发失败状态，或是进入超过5年没有任何新进展的停滞状态。从研发终止前的进度来看，有167个管线研发终止于药物发现或临床前阶段，占比达到64.4%，其次是临床II期阶段，终止管线占比15.8%，小核酸药物的研发难点高度集中在早期转化与临床价值验证环节。数据来源：摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库小核酸药物前期研究向正式立项的转化概率较低，候选药物常脱靶导致毒性是重要原因之一。从整体研究终止的原因来看，早期研究未商业化/临床前未推进是占比最大的原因，合计占比32%。根据奥尼兰姆数据，约有40%的Galnac-siRNA候选序列在临床前的大鼠独立筛选阶段中因为肝毒性而被淘汰，而这一肝毒性是siRNA与非目标RNA发生seed区脱靶配对导致的，可见对于小核酸药物，靶向递送与精准识别是药物研发前期阻碍推进的重大壁垒。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》2. 临床阶段小核酸药物推进壁垒临床阶段小核酸药物最大推进壁垒在于证明其临床价值。从不同研发阶段的终止原因分布来看，药物研发前期（药物发现、临床前）的管线，最常因战略管线优先级调整、早期研究未商业化等原因终止；而进入临床阶段后，因疗效不足、未达主要终点终止的管线占比开始显著上升。即便项目成功完成立项推进到临床，小核酸药物仍容易在临床阶段暴露临床获益不足的问题，这也表明行业在立项前的调研预测工作，仍然存在较大的优化空间。二、小核酸药物研发高失败率靶点分布在近年失败的259个管线中，有83个管线未公布其具体靶点。在剩余有靶点信息的失败管线中，涉及靶点135个，整体靶点集中度较低，较少有明显的“陷阱”靶点。但其中仍有20个靶点的开发失败率超过60%，ICAM1、SCNN1A等9个靶点失败率高达100%，体现出相当高的开发难度。1. DMD：研发热情与失败率双高DMD靶点同时具有高研发热情与高失败率。作为杜氏肌营养不良症的核心靶点，近5年有32个管线针对DMD进行研发，但失败率高达62.5%，有20个管线宣告失败。其中，BioMarin、WAVE Life Sciences曾分别将管线推进至II期与III期临床，但均因疗效不达预期而终止研发。2. TLR9：跨领域开发的高难度样本TLR9靶点作为免疫通路中的关键蛋白，近五年同样拥有较高的研发热情，目标适应症横跨癌症、呼吸系统、胃肠道、炎症、神经系统、免疫调节、皮肤病、肌肉骨骼系统与血液系统等多个领域，但其失败率同样高达62.5%（8个研发管线中5个失败）。Karolinska曾将对应药物cobitollmod推进至III期临床，但因无法达成临床终点而全面终止开发。三、小核酸药物研发失败代表性案例盘点梳理上述失败管线不难发现，两类问题最为典型：其一，靶点被成功调控，并不意味着疾病进程能够被改变；其二，药效成立之后，安全窗口与产品价值仍决定研发成败。以下四个案例，正是这两类困境的缩影。场景一：靶点调控实现，不等于疾病进程得到改善1. 案例一：WVE-004（C9orf72靶点，ASO）WVE-004是Wave Life Sciences开发的一款靶向C9orf72的ASO药物，适应症为C9orf72相关肌萎缩侧索硬化（ALS）和额颞叶痴呆（FTD），最高研发阶段为Phase I/II。C9orf72基因中的六核苷酸重复扩增是ALS和FTD最常见的遗传病因之一，其异常转录产物poly(GP)被认为具有神经毒性。WVE-004的设计逻辑是通过降解含有异常扩增的C9orf72转录本，降低poly(GP)水平，从而减轻神经毒性。临床前研究中，WVE-004能够有效降低患者来源神经细胞的poly-GP，且保留正常转录本；小鼠实验中，药品展现了长期药效，成功降低脊髓与皮层的poly-GP。2022年临床试验中，实验组出现了显著的poly-GP下降，但神经损伤标记NFL及临床功能没有显著改善，公司选择继续推进实验。2023年，在更多患者入组与进行更长期试验后，NFL与临床功能依然没有出现显著改善，公司宣布终止研发。研发时间轴：2018年：临床前研究2021年：启动临床I/II期2023年：临床结束，宣布终止研发失败启示：即使靶点调控获得预期结果，其距离最终疾病获益仍然有着距离。2. 案例二：BIIB105（ION541，ATXN2靶点，ASO）BIIB105是Ionis授权Biogen开发的一款靶向ATXN2的ASO药物，同样用于ALS治疗。ATXN2编码ataxin-2蛋白，其多聚谷氨酰胺扩增与ALS风险相关，被认为通过促进TDP-43蛋白的异常聚集参与疾病进程。临床前小鼠实验中，通过遗传学手段降低ATXN2或使用ATXN2 ASO均能显著降低TDP-43聚集并延长小鼠生存时间，展现出强大的临床潜力。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》2020年启动的I/II期ALSpire研究（n=99）中，BIIB105实现了脑脊液中ATXN2蛋白的统计学显著降低。然而，在6个月的安慰剂对照期内，BIIB105未能降低血浆神经丝轻链（NfL）水平——NfL是神经退行性变和神经元损伤的标志物。功能、呼吸和肌力等临床终点同样没有改善。在超过40周的开放标签扩展随访中，ATXN2的持续降低并未转化为NfL或临床功能的任何改善。2024年5月，Biogen和Ionis宣布终止BIIB105的开发。研发时间轴：2013年：Ionis授权Biogen开发2020年：启动临床I/II期2024年：宣布终止研发失败原因：靶向机制明确且在人体内展现积极信号，但未能转化为疾病获益。失败启示：与WVE-004类似，即使设计的路径在动物模型中获得了积极结果，靶点调控也达到预期，但距离最终的患者获益仍存在较大差距。小核酸药物的新靶点开发仍然有着巨大的不确定性。场景二：药效达标，安全窗口与产品价值决定研发成败3. 案例三：SRP-5051（DMD外显子51跳跃，肽偶联PMO）SRP-5051（vesleteplirsen）是Sarepta开发的一款多肽偶联PMO（PPMO）药物，通过诱导DMD基因外显子51跳跃、恢复抗肌萎缩蛋白表达来治疗杜氏肌营养不良症。与WVE-004和BIIB105不同，SRP-5051在临床试验中展现了明确的疗效信号。在II期MOMENTUM研究的Part A中，SRP-5051观察到了显著的外显子跳跃和肌营养不良蛋白表达上升，且呈现剂量依赖关系，药物在试验过程中呈现良好的可耐受性，未出现显著的安全性信号。在Part B中，公司继续推高剂量，并于2021年观察到了显著优于已上市外显子跳跃药物的跳跃水平和肌营养不良蛋白表达水平。但随之而来的是安全性问题。早在研究早期，低镁血症（血镁水平偏低）的风险就已被识别，当时被判断为“可监测、可管理”。然而在后续研究中，部分患者出现了持续性的低镁血症，且即使在停药后仍然存在，同时伴有eGFR下降（肾功能指标恶化）。2024年11月，Sarepta宣布终止SRP-5051的开发，理由是长期安全性和耐受性的考量。SRP-5051的失败提供了一个与前述神经领域案例截然不同的教训：当疗效已经成立，安全窗口便成为产品价值的唯一裁判。外显子跳跃水平和肌营养不良蛋白表达的数据是令人鼓舞的，但持续性的低镁血症和肾功能下降意味着药物的治疗窗口过窄——在能够产生疗效的剂量下，安全性风险超出了可接受的范围。这一案例的核心启示在于：对于早期出现的安全性问题，应当尽早评估其剂量依赖性和可逆性，避免在研发后期因安全性风险积累而导致全部投入付诸东流。4. 案例四：Vupanorsen（ANGPTL3靶点，GalNAc-ASO）Vupanorsen是Ionis发现、辉瑞引进的GalNAc-ASO药物，靶向ANGPTL3，适应症为血脂异常与心代谢疾病，最高研发阶段推进至IIb期临床。ANGPTL3是一个经过人类遗传学充分验证的靶点——ANGPTL3功能缺失突变携带者具有较低的LDL-C、甘油三酯水平和冠心病风险。2016年的临床I期试验中，实验组体内ANGPTL3的表达下降83%，同时带来甘油三酯最大平均下降66%、LDL-C最大平均下降35%的显著结果。进入临床IIa期试验后，主要终点再次达标，甘油三酯相较安慰剂组下降约44%，non-HDL-C下降约18%，总胆固醇下降约19%，但LDL-C对比安慰剂组没有出现显著下降，脂肪肝、糖代谢指标等也没有得到显著改善。进入IIb期试验后，在加大药物剂量后获得了更显著的ANGPTL3与甘油三酯下降结果，但non-HDL-C仅下降约22-27.7%，LDL-C仅下降8%-16%，ApoB下降约6-15%，同时加大药量后出现了部分肝脏安全性问题，最终公司宣布终止研发。 研发时间轴：2013年：药物发现2015年：启动临床I期2017年：临床IIa期（高脂血症、脂肪肝）2018年：临床I/II期2019年：辉瑞引进开发2020年：临床IIb期（高脂血症）2022年：宣布终止研发失败原因：尽管证实能够导向临床获益，但获益不足使得药物缺乏继续开发的价值。这款药物的失败留给行业的启示是，即便已经有上市药品Evinacumab证明该靶点整体成药性可行，临床结果也证明药物的作用机制能够带来部分指标改善，但如果最终的临床获益与药物最初的开发期望存在明显差距，不足以支撑药物最终走向上市。结语复盘近五年小核酸失败管线不难发现，研发风险贯穿从临床前到 II 期临床的全流程，失败诱因已经从早期单纯的递送难题，逐步转向靶点生物学验证、分子信号向临床获益转化、安全窗口评估等更深层问题。但失败不是小核酸药物故事的反面，而是它的一部分。对于药企研发人员、项目决策者而言，依托摩熵医药数据库持续对标同靶点、同递送技术、同适应症项目的临床推进节奏与终止案例，读懂靶点冷热与失败底层逻辑，才能在管线立项、临床方案设计阶段识别潜在风险，提升小核酸药物研发的成功率。相关拓展阅读：1. title: Blood Cancer Discov：三重靶向＋OX40增强＋6天快速制造！三特异性CAR T细胞疗法为复发难治B细胞血液癌症带来新希望
content:
Blood Cancer Discov：三重靶向＋OX40增强＋6天快速制造！三特异性CAR T细胞疗法为复发难治B细胞血液癌症带来新希望
来源：生物谷原创 2026-10-22 10:02
由俄亥俄州立大学综合癌症中心领导的一项I期临床试验结果显示，可能有一条途径可改善复发或治疗耐药性B细胞血液癌症患者的治疗选择。研究结果发表在Blood Cancer Discovery上。
研究人员得以在早期工作的基础上进一步推进，该早期工作利用CAR T细胞疗法增强B细胞血液癌症的治疗。所有血液癌症中约一半为B细胞血液癌症，包括淋巴瘤和某些白血病。
该试验测试了靶向3种蛋白——CD19、CD20和CD22的三特异性CAR T细胞疗法，并使用一种名为OX40的不同蛋白来增强患者的免疫反应。
“这是CAR T细胞临床试验首次使用OX-40来增强该过程并改善肿瘤杀伤，”该研究第一作者兼通讯作者Sumithira Vasu医学博士说。“我们试验的结果可能为那些B细胞血液癌症复发或治疗停止起效后选择有限的患者带来更好的治疗结局。”
团队还使用了一种更快的流程，在短短6天内完成细胞的采集、制备和回输给患者。这带来了积极结局，且患者副作用极小。
“此前有观点认为新鲜细胞回输更可取，而我们能够证明快速制造时间和新鲜细胞回输的可行性，”共同资深作者LHM项目成员Lapo Alinari医学博士、哲学博士说。“这在B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤中产生了有意义的临床活性且副作用极小，并在套细胞淋巴瘤、滤泡性淋巴瘤和弥漫性大B细胞淋巴瘤中实现了缓解。”
CAR T细胞疗法如何工作？
CAR T细胞疗法从患者免疫系统中取出抗癌T细胞，在实验室中修改这些细胞以增强其杀死癌细胞的能力，然后通过输注将细胞回输给患者。
该细胞疗法通常靶向在B细胞血液癌症中起重要作用的CD19蛋白。在此前的动物研究中，其他机构的科学家开发了一种同时靶向另外2种蛋白——CD20和CD22的CAR T细胞疗法，并显示出更强的有效性。
“尽管CAR T细胞疗法已经彻底改变了B细胞血液癌症患者的治疗，缓解率高，但许多患者会在CAR T细胞疗法后复发，且往往在第1年内，”Vasu说。“患者随后只剩下有限的治疗选择。”
该临床试验入组了18名中位年龄为64岁的患者，其中16人接受了OX-40蛋白增强的CAR T细胞过程治疗。所有入组患者在接受增强细胞疗法之前，此前均已接受过中位3种类型的治疗。
“虽然我们的试验显示，接受增强CAR T细胞治疗的B细胞非霍奇金淋巴瘤患者取得了令人鼓舞的结局，但仍需要在更大患者群体中进行更多研究，”资深共同作者Marcos de Lima医学博士说。（生物谷Bioon.com）

10月20日，石药集团宣布，其自主开发的SYH2083滴眼液治疗干眼症的Ⅰ期临床试验（SYH2083-001）已在中国正式启动，目前正推进受试者招募及筛选工作。图源：石药集团企业公告SYH2083是一款靶向淋巴细胞功能相关抗原1（LFA-1）和活性醛类物质（RASP）的双靶点抑制剂。摩熵医药数据库显示，该产品于2026年9月7日首次获批临床，并于10月20日正式启动Ⅰ期临床试验。该产品可抑制LFA-1与细胞间黏附分子-1（ICAM-1）的相互作用，减少LFA-1介导的细胞黏附，同时捕获活性醛类物质。通过双靶点协同作用，该产品有望改善单靶点药物在安全性和有效性方面的局限，为干眼症治疗提供新的潜在选择。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库此次启动的SYH2083-001研究是一项在中国健康参与者中开展的单中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照、剂量递增Ⅰ期临床试验，主要评估该产品单次及多次给药后的安全性、耐受性和药代动力学特征。随着Ⅰ期临床试验启动，SYH2083将进一步开展早期临床研究，其安全性及药代动力学表现有待后续试验验证。参考来源：[1] 企业公告/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 石药集团首款三抗SYS6088与ADC新药SYS6062同日获批临床，晚期实体瘤布局双线加速2. 石药集团连发三条研发重磅进展！mRNA肿瘤疫苗、带状疱疹疫苗FDA临床许可、减重单抗Ib期同步落地3. 石药集团SYS6010拟纳入突破性治疗品种，EGFR ADC第4项BTD落地，剑指驱动基因阴性非鳞状NSCLC

content:
分子检测是实现晚期非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）精准治疗的前提，但全球范围内驱动基因的检测周转时间与治疗启动时机的差异仍影响着临床结局。 该研究揭示了检测时效对治疗决策的影响，也为临床优化诊疗路径、把握治疗时机以改善患者预后提供了依据。 EGFR突变在白种人群和亚洲人群中的发生率分别为5%～20%和40%～55%。

title: 康缘药业中药1.1类新药十味安肠颗粒获批临床，靶向溃疡性结肠炎新赛道
content:
10月20日，摩熵医药中国药品审评数据库显示，康缘药业联合图锋医药、北峰药业及上海中医药大学申报的中药1.1类新药十味安肠颗粒获批临床，拟用于溃疡性结肠炎。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库一、聚焦溃疡性结肠炎，康缘再推创新中药十味安肠颗粒由江苏康缘药业股份有限公司联合上海图锋医药科技有限公司、辽宁北峰药业有限公司及上海中医药大学共同研发，是一款基于中医临床经验方开发的现代中药颗粒制剂。据摩熵医药数据库显示，该药于2026年8月12日首次提交临床试验申请，受理号为CXZL2600075，并于10月20日首次获批临床。图源：摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库此次获批的适应症为溃疡性结肠炎。作为中药1.1类创新药，十味安肠颗粒后续临床研究进展及疗效、安全性数据值得关注。康缘药业在肠道疾病领域已有其他创新中药布局。公司另一款中药1.1类新药健脾疏肝固本颗粒此前已获得临床试验默示许可，拟用于腹泻型肠易激综合征（肝郁脾虚证）。两款产品针对不同适应症，体现了公司在中药创新药领域的持续布局。在成熟中成药方面，康缘药业拥有天舒胶囊、天舒片、苁蓉总苷胶囊等独家产品，属于神经系统疾病用药领域。摩熵医药数据库显示，天舒胶囊2025年全终端销售额超过2亿元，2026年上半年销售额约0.68亿元。

title: 南京正大天晴左卡尼汀咀嚼片获批上市！斩获国内首仿+首家过评，撬动超6亿元市场
content:
10月15日，NMPA官网显示，南京正大天晴制药申报的左卡尼汀咀嚼片获批上市，成为该剂型国内首仿。摩熵医药数据库显示，2026年上半年，左卡尼汀相关剂型在全终端销售额超过6亿元。在这一市场规模下，咀嚼片剂型迎来首家国内企业获批，南京正大天晴进一步丰富了其仿制药产品矩阵。图源：NMPA官网一、超6亿元市场，咀嚼片剂型迎来首仿左卡尼汀是一种参与人体能量代谢的药物，主要作用是促进长链脂肪酸进入线粒体进行β-氧化，为心肌、骨骼肌等组织提供能量。其原研企业为意大利阿尔法西格玛公司，左卡尼汀于1990年获得美国FDA批准上市，左卡尼汀注射液原研产品于1999年在国内上市。摩熵医药数据库显示，左卡尼汀注射液、片剂、口服溶液等相关剂型，2026年上半年全终端销售额超过6亿元，已形成一定的市场规模。

title: 派诺生物三款疟疾多阶段疫苗伦理获批，将在澳大利亚启动I期首次人体（First in Human, FIH）临床试验！
content:
派诺生物三款疟疾多阶段疫苗伦理获批，将在澳大利亚启动I期首次人体（First in Human, FIH）临床试验
来源：生物谷 2026-10-22 15:51
Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准派诺生物在澳大利亚开展首次人体临床试验，评估其针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫的多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗。
Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准派诺生物在澳大利亚开展首次人体临床试验，评估其针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫的多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗。
派诺生物是一家致力于开发下一代疫苗、以满足全球未满足医疗需求的生物技术公司。公司宣布，其三款多阶段新型U-VLP®疟疾候选疫苗的I期首次人体临床试验（NCT07831226）已于2026年10月19日获得Bellberry 人类研究伦理委员会批准。
其中，LYB014针对恶性疟原虫（Plasmodium falciparum）生命周期中的三个关键阶段；LYB017针对间日疟原虫（Plasmodium vivax）生命周期中的三个关键阶段；而LYB027则同时针对恶性疟原虫和间日疟原虫生命周期中的上述三个关键阶段。这些候选疫苗将联合派诺生物自研的A02佐剂进行评估。A02是一种新型脂质体佐剂，其活性成分均为合成物质。
这项随机、双盲、对照、剂量递增的临床试验将在澳大利亚墨尔本的Nucleus Network Pty Ltd.开展，旨在评估上述疫苗在健康成年志愿者中的安全性和免疫原性。首例受试者入组预计将于2026年12月完成。免疫原性分析将与设于牛津大学儿科学系（Department of Paediatrics）的Draper实验室合作开展。
这些疫苗由派诺生物开发，旨在满足对新一代疟疾疫苗的需求。其设计针对疟原虫生命周期中的三个关键阶段，并期望通过预防感染、发病和传播，为未来消除疟疾的长远目标作出贡献。
尽管全球抗疟工作已取得显著进展，疟疾仍是严峻的全球性公共卫生威胁。2024 年，全球预估疟疾病例 2.82 亿例，死亡 61 万人。绝大多数病例由恶性疟原虫（P. falciparum）和间日疟原虫（P. vivax）两种主要疟原虫引发。两类疟原虫具备复杂的生命周期：携带病原体的蚊虫叮咬人体后，孢子体随之侵入机体并迁移至肝脏完成发育（第一阶段）；随后进入血液循环、入侵红细胞大量增殖（第二阶段）；部分虫体将分化至有性生殖阶段，当蚊虫吸食感染者血液时，虫体进入蚊体内继续发育，继而传播至新宿主（第三阶段）。
目前，世界卫生组织（WHO）批准使用的RTS,S/AS01和R21/Matrix-M疟疾疫苗仅针对恶性疟原虫生命周期的第一阶段，既往在儿童群体开展的 II/III 期临床试验中，仅展现出针对临床疟疾的部分保护效力。LYB014、LYB017和LYB027的研发理念在于探索：同时针对疟原虫生命周期各阶段以及/或覆盖多个疟原虫种类，是否能够提供互补且层次化的保护作用。该科学假说将在后续临床试验中进一步评估。
牛津大学疫苗与转化医学教授Simon Draper表示："我们很高兴能与派诺生物合作，共同开展这项首次人体临床试验的免疫原性分析工作。疟疾仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战，因此有必要持续探索创新疫苗策略，以在疟原虫生命周期的多个阶段提供更广泛、更持久的保护。"
"我们的科研技术有潜力变革抗击疟疾的方式，"派诺生物首席执行官晋博士表示，"我们开发的疟疾疫苗和A02佐剂的目标不仅是预防感染，更是要创造一个更强大、更可负担的防护盾，以应对抗疟原虫复杂的生物学特性，这可能是迈向最终消除疟疾的关键一步。"

小核酸药物正从罕见病与遗传病的小众应用场景，稳步拓展至肿瘤、心血管及代谢疾病等更广阔的疾病治疗版图，是当下创新药研发领域最具发展潜力的方向之一。该类药物以10—50个核苷酸组成的短链核酸分子为活性成分，能够突破传统药物“难以成药”的靶点壁垒，通过降解、沉默或抑制特定基因表达，从源头调控疾病发生机制，同时具备作用效率高、研发周期短、平台可复用等独特优势。当前小核酸药物已形成反义寡核苷酸（ASO）、小干扰 RNA（siRNA）、微小 RNA（miRNA）、适体（Aptamer）四大主流品类。依托化学修饰、GalNAc偶联、LNP包载、抗体/多肽偶联等多元化递送技术的持续迭代，其临床应用边界不断拓宽，全面覆盖肿瘤、眼科疾病、中枢神经系统疾病、遗传及罕见病、心血管及代谢性疾病五大核心领域，全球潜在市场规模约8500亿美元。凭借持续升级的技术体系与不断落地的临床价值，小核酸药物已然成为继小分子药物、抗体药物之后又一值得长期关注的新药研发热点。本文核心内容均摘编自摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》报告。该报告依托摩熵医药数据库海量生物医药全产业链数据，从技术概览、行业沿革、市场格局、在研管线、终止研发管线等多个维度，系统梳理行业发展全貌，精准研判研发热点与潜在风险，深度挖掘赛道增长潜力。本文结合前沿技术特征与产业落地现状，系统整合并梳理了小核酸药物的技术体系、临床应用场景、主流递送技术及行业发展核心挑战。一、小核酸药物概览：技术分类与核心价值小核酸药物（small nucleic acid drugs）是由10—50个核苷酸构成的短链核酸分子，按药理载荷可分为反义寡核苷酸（ASO）、小干扰RNA（siRNA）、微小RNA（miRNA）与适体（Aptamer）药物等。作为核酸药物的一类，小核酸药物具有作用效率高、研发周期较短等特点，已成为新药研发领域的研究热点。1. 主要分类ASO（反义寡核苷酸）：结构上通常为单链的寡核苷酸；通过与靶RNA序列互补结合，实现RNA降解、剪接调控或翻译阻断的目的。siRNA（小干扰RNA）：通常为双链RNA；经RISC复合物介导，特异性降解靶RNA，实现基因沉默。miRNA（微小RNA）：miRNA类药物可通过模拟或抑制内源性miRNA，调控相关基因表达网络。Aptamer（适体药物）：化学本质常为DNA或RNA，通过特定三维空间构象与靶标结合，蛋白质是目前最常见的靶标。2. 作用机制小核酸药物的作用机制主要分为两类：（1）基因表达调控型：以ASO、siRNA和miRNA为代表，通过靶RNA识别，实现RNA降解或剪接调控，进而改变蛋白表达水平。（2）靶标直接结合型：以适体药物为代表，通过核酸链折叠形成三维构象，直接结合蛋白或细胞等靶标，阻断或调节靶点功能。3. 临床价值这种特殊的作用模式也赋予了小核酸药物显著的临床价值：它能够针对传统药物难以成药的靶点，大幅拓展疾病治疗的边界；序列设计具备天然的平台复用性，企业可以基于同一技术框架快速拓展新靶点与新适应症；在遗传病、罕见病及常见慢性病领域都展现出极高的应用潜力；部分成熟技术路线的产品还能实现数月一次的长效给药，部分前沿研究甚至在向接近一次性治疗的目标推进。4. 关键挑战目前小核酸药物行业仍处于高速发展期，技术落地与产业化仍面临多重瓶颈。首先，药物有效成分体内稳定性不足，极易被体内核酸酶降解，直接影响药效发挥；其次，组织与细胞特异性递送是行业核心技术瓶颈，严重制约药物生物利用率与靶向精准度；再次，药物应用存在脱靶效应、非特异性免疫激活及长期安全性未知等风险，临床应用安全性仍需持续验证；最后，药物生产工艺复杂，生产成本、质量控制及规模化量产的技术标准严苛，产业化门槛较高。整体来看，未来小核酸药物的行业竞争，将集中聚焦于靶点精准筛选、高效递送技术突破、用药安全性优化三大核心方向。二、小核酸药物的主要治疗领域小核酸药物横跨肿瘤、眼科疾病、中枢神经系统、遗传病及罕见病、心血管及代谢性疾病五大市场，潜在市场规模约8500亿美元，展现出广阔的应用潜力。图片来源：摩熵咨询《小核酸药物的下一站——全球研发演进、技术迭代与研发成败洞察》心血管及代谢性疾病（2400亿美元市场）：高胆固醇血症、高甘油三酯血症、高血压、血栓疾病等。遗传病及罕见病（2358亿美元市场）：血友病A/B、遗传性血管性水肿、肝性卟啉症、家族性淀粉样变多发性神经病等。中枢神经系统（334亿美元市场）：肌萎缩侧索硬化、运动神经元病等。眼科疾病（600亿美元市场）：地图状萎缩、年龄相关性黄斑变性、湿性年龄相关性黄斑变性、巨细胞病毒视网膜炎等。肿瘤（2864亿美元市场）：骨髓发育异常综合征、胰腺癌等。其他：角膜移植排斥、慢性疲劳综合征等。目前，小核酸药物已经在心血管及代谢性疾病、遗传病、罕见病等领域展现出较高的应用潜力。以肌萎缩侧索硬化（渐冻症）为例，该疾病由超氧化物歧化酶1（SOD1）基因突变引发，传统药物研发长期陷入困境，核心原因是SOD1蛋白结构高度稳定，无适配传统药物结合的作用位点，始终缺乏有效治疗手段。而小核酸药物托夫生（Tofersen）可直接靶向致病基因与RNA，从疾病根源干预病情发展，为渐冻症治疗开辟全新路径。该药物于2023年获批上市，2024年正式进入中国市场，落地惠及国内罕见病患者，充分印证了小核酸药物的独特临床价值。三、小核酸药物的主要递送方式递送技术被普遍视为小核酸药物研发的核心胜负手。当前上市产品以化学修饰及GalNAc偶联最为常见，同时以LNP（脂质纳米颗粒）及抗体/多肽偶联探索肝外靶向。1. 化学修饰直接给药主要用于ASO与适体药物，常见给药部位为玻璃体内、鞘内、皮下与局部。其核心逻辑是依靠PS／2’位修饰或PEG化增强稳定性，无需复杂载体。作为最成熟的技术路线，它特别适合局部用药或可直接到达靶组织的场景，代表药品包括Fomivirsen、Nusinersen、Tofersen（托夫生）与Pegaptanib。2. GalNAc偶联主要用于以siRNA为主、部分ASO的药物，靶向肝细胞ASGPR，可实现皮下注射、低频给药与明确的肝靶向，是当前肝靶向小核酸的核心平台。代表产品包括Givosiran、Lumasiran、Inclisiran（英克司兰钠）、Vutrisiran与Eplontersen。3. LNP包载主要用于以siRNA为主、部分miRNA及双链RNA的探索。其递送逻辑是包载保护核酸，促进细胞摄取与内体逃逸，适用于需要系统给药、需要额外包载保护的RNA载荷。其系统性递送验证充分，但产品数量少于GalNAc，代表产品为Patisiran。4. 抗体/多肽偶联主要用于ASO与siRNA，目标是突破肝外组织，聚焦肌肉、心肌及中枢神经系统；其核心价值在于利用受体介导内吞实现细胞定向递送。该路线临床推进较快，是肝外递送的重要方向，代表在研项目包括Del-desiran（AOC 1001）、DYNE-101等。需要补充的是，化学修饰是多数小核酸药物的技术基础，与LNP或偶联策略并非互斥关系——GalNAc-siRNA、LNP-siRNA通常同样采用2’位修饰及磷硫酰键等化学修饰手段。递送方式的演进也并非简单的代际替代，而是在用药便利性、靶向可及目标等方向上的持续拓展。除上述四种方式外，外泌体、无机纳米颗粒（金、氧化铁、硅等）等多种递送策略也处于探索之中。结语从首个反义药物问世，到GalNAc技术平台的成熟，再到抗体偶联递送向肝外组织进军，小核酸药物已完成从“概念验证”到“商业化兑现”的关键跨越。展望未来，靶点选择的精准化、递送系统的组织拓展化、化学修饰与安全性优化的持续迭代，将共同决定这一赛道的下一批赢家。对于身处其中的研发者与决策者而言，唯有建立在对全球研发数据持续追踪与深入洞察之上的判断，才能在技术迭代与研发成败交织的浪潮中把握先机。资料来源：1. title: 齐鲁制药1类创新生物药QLS2401获批临床，靶向三靶点布局前列腺癌免疫治疗
content:
10月14日，摩熵医药中国药品审评数据库显示，齐鲁制药自主研发的1类创新生物药QLS2401注射液获得国家药品监督管理局药品审评中心（CDE）临床试验默示许可，拟用于治疗转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库QLS2401是一款同时靶向PSMA、STEAP1和CD3的三特异性T细胞衔接器（TCE）。其通过双肿瘤抗原识别与T细胞募集相结合的设计，探索前列腺癌免疫治疗的新路径。此次获准开展临床试验，意味着QLS2401进入临床开发阶段。其双靶点设计能否在肿瘤抗原表达异质性等情况下展现优势，还有待后续临床研究验证。一、三靶点设计，探索前列腺癌免疫治疗新路径转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌是前列腺癌治疗中的重要挑战之一，患者仍存在未被满足的治疗需求。QLS2401采用三特异性T细胞衔接器设计，同时识别肿瘤相关抗原PSMA、STEAP1，并结合T细胞表面的CD3，旨在将T细胞募集至肿瘤细胞附近，激活T细胞介导的肿瘤杀伤作用。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库与仅针对单一肿瘤抗原的策略相比，PSMA与STEAP1双靶点设计有望提高对不同抗原表达状态肿瘤细胞的识别能力，并降低单一抗原表达下降所导致的免疫逃逸风险。此外，QLS2401还通过优化CD3亲和力及肿瘤抗原结合设计，尝试在增强抗肿瘤活性的同时优化分子特性。不过，这些设计能否转化为更好的疗效和安全性，仍需临床数据进一步验证。二、临床前研究显示潜力，低抗原表达模型值得关注根据现有临床前研究数据，QLS2401在不同抗原表达水平的肿瘤模型中展现出一定的抗肿瘤活性。在PSMA或STEAP1中等、低表达的细胞模型中，QLS2401的杀伤活性优于同类对照分子。在细胞系来源异种移植（CDX）和患者来源异种移植（PDX）肿瘤模型中，该药也表现出抗肿瘤活性，尤其在低抗原表达模型中显示出相对优势。这些结果为QLS2401的双靶点设计提供了临床前依据，也使其在肿瘤抗原表达异质性方面的潜在价值受到关注。但需要指出，临床前模型的结果不能直接预测人体中的疗效。QLS2401能否在患者中实现有效的肿瘤控制，以及其安全性、耐受性和适用人群如何，仍有待临床试验回答。三、今年19款生物药获批临床，齐鲁制药持续拓展创新管线QLS2401的临床获批，也是齐鲁制药今年生物药研发进展的一部分。据相关统计，2026年以来，齐鲁制药已有25余款1类新药获批临床，其中19款为生物药1类新药。上述19款生物药中，13款为首次获批临床的新品，覆盖双靶点融合蛋白、双抗及多抗、抗体偶联药物（ADC）等多个研发方向。

title: 石药集团首款三抗SYS6088与ADC新药SYS6062同日获批临床，晚期实体瘤布局双线加速
content:
10月15日，石药集团宣布，集团开发的SYS6088注射液和SYS6062均获NMPA批准开展临床试验，拟用于晚期实体瘤。图源：企业公告其中，SYS6088是石药集团布局的首个三特异性抗体（以下简称“三抗”），靶向PD-1、VEGFA和CTLA-4。随着这一产品获批临床，石药集团正式进入三抗研发赛道。一、首个三抗获批临床，聚焦三靶点协同SYS6088是一款PD-1/VEGFA/CTLA-4三特异性抗体，本次获批临床拟单药用于晚期/转移性实体瘤。摩熵医药数据库显示，该品种在2026年9月首次申请临床，10月15日，石药集团宣布获批临床。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从作用机制来看，该产品试图通过同时作用于三个靶点，协同调节肿瘤免疫微环境。其中，PD-1和CTLA-4均与T细胞免疫调控有关，VEGFA则参与肿瘤血管生成及肿瘤微环境调节。通过整合上述靶点，SYS6088旨在兼顾解除免疫抑制、促进T细胞活化与扩增，以及抑制肿瘤血管生成等作用。此外，该产品还对Fc端进行了改造，以降低潜在毒性风险并延长药物半衰期。据披露，临床前研究显示，SYS6088在多种恶性肿瘤模型中表现出抗肿瘤活性。至于其多靶点设计能否转化为临床疗效优势，以及安全性是否能够得到验证，仍有待后续临床研究回答。二、三抗与ADC同步推进，石药集团丰富肿瘤管线截至目前，石药集团已有70余款1类新药处于获批临床及以上阶段。除SYS6088外，石药集团另一款新药SYS6062也于同日获NMPA批准在中国开展临床试验，拟用于晚期实体瘤。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库SYS6062是一款抗体偶联药物（ADC），通过抗体识别肿瘤细胞相关靶点，将细胞毒性载荷递送至细胞内，以发挥抗肿瘤作用。临床前研究显示，该产品在多种癌症模型中表现出抗肿瘤活性。从三抗到ADC，两款新药采用了不同的抗肿瘤策略。其中，SYS6088聚焦多靶点免疫调节，SYS6062则通过抗体实现细胞毒性载荷的靶向递送。

title: BMS领投Pathos AI 2.37亿美元E轮融资并达成阿尔茨海默病合作【AI生成】
content:
生物技术公司Pathos AI宣布完成由制药巨头百时美施贵宝（BMS）领投的2.37亿美元E轮融资，并于同日与BMS及Tempus AI签署聚焦神经退行性疾病（特别是阿尔茨海默病）的合作协议。Pathos利用其Foundry人工智能平台加速临床开发并降低风险。根据合作条款，Pathos将向Tempus支付5500万美元用于获取涵盖数十万神经系统疾病患者的综合数据集，以指导适应性临床试验。Foundry平台通过整合基因组学至竞争格局等多维数据，提供实时“持续情报”以辅助药物研发决策。此外，Pathos正利用该融资推进肿瘤管线，包括Alphamab Oncology授权的TROP2/HER3双特异性抗体偶联药物（ADC）、AstraZeneca合作的PROTAC以及DeuterOncology的MET激酶抑制剂等，部分资金也将用于扩展Foundry平台规模。

content:
本期【来问讲者】邀请 夸克医药医学总监马瑞，成都纽瑞特医疗注册负责人吴文轩，中国核工业集团有限公司科技带头人、中国同辐股份有限公司首席专家李洪玉，赛赋医药副总裁、赛赋国通(无锡) 傅鹏，夸克医药市场总监、DIA中国放射性药物学术社区秘书孟祥和 ，结合各自的专业背景与实践经验，围绕放射性药物研发与临床转化中的关键问题展开分享，探讨新技术发展对临床研究的影响、创新核药研发中的监管沟通与非临床评价挑战，以及行业快速发展背景下专业交流与人才能力建设的重要性，为放射性药物创新研发与临床转化提供多元视角和实践参考。 随着AI、个体化剂量学和真实世界证据不断发展，未来放射性药物临床研究会发生哪些变化。 《2026 DIA 放射性药物进阶培训：从新型核素研发到临床转化实践》课程讲者。
